name: Reference cube (REFCUBE) incl. dual-cube mode
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Reference data must share the main data's spatial dimensions. It can be an in-memory 2D/3D array, an image cube file (refnt = 1 or nt, any refnlp), or an [imcube, spcube] pair (dual-cube mode, v1.6) that gets its own spectral displays; array-valued keywords set main and reference separately. Main-to-reference maps come from the WCS or a linear fallback, and tutorials load a Level-3-formatted AIA cube as reference.
gap: No preset opens a reference (an AIA cutout or a second window) with its own displays: the WP4 prototype opens only sjis[0], a rasters[0] map and one profile (wp4_common.py:180-199). WP1's test pairings (716-718) leave out local AIA cutout to IRIS. A linear fallback without WCS is absent, but IRIS L2 data always carry WCS.
glue_evidence: Released glue 1.27.0 wcs_autolinking.py:318-320 only autolinks BaseHighLevelWCS coords, so glue-solar's low-level _GlueWCS (glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:35,75@main 236f0a8) is skipped. Core #2595 gives one SJI/raster WCS link (IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260923/README.md:19-25). No linear-rescale link helper exists (glue/core/link_helpers.py:25-31,341 in .venv 1.27.0). Aligned AIA cutouts load as SJI-format cubes (loaders/iris.py:121-125; scan.py:110-115,174-175@main).
suggested_home: WP4 (reference/second-window preset) + WP1 (add AIA-cutout pairing to link tests)
rationale: For IRIS the reference is AIA context or a second spectral window. Generic Glue datasets, viewers and links already carry most of it, so this is layout work in WP4, not new machinery.
verify_note: Classification holds: no reference-window or second-window preset exists, and WP1's pairing list omits local AIA cutout to IRIS. The line cite is slightly off: the autolink check is at wcs_autolinking.py:320-321, not 318-320. 'No linear fallback' is true for the GUI, but core has a programmatic AffineLink (wcs_autolinking.py:37), and users can add their own @link_function.

name: Load reference and SJI cubes at runtime (File > Open)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: File > Open loads SJI cubes (v1.7.1) and reference image or image+spectral cubes (v1.7.2) after start-up, even when none were given at launch. Channels can therefore be added or switched without restarting.
gap: Loading works. The WP4 time links are created only inside quicklook() (wp4_common.py:169-178), and the plan does not say how datasets added after the preset get paired or time-linked. AIA cutouts opened by File > Open bypass the IRIS factory (is_iris_fits needs TELESCOP=='IRIS', iris.py:16-20); a real cutout's TELESCOP was not verified.
glue_evidence: File > Open Data Set exists (glue_qt/app/application.py:874-877@origin/main 9780eaf9). The IRIS factory read_iris_file (glue_solar/sources/iris.py:23-28@main) and the browser menu plugin (iris.py:47-65) load SJI/raster at any time. Released core does not autolink them (wcs_autolinking.py:318-320).
plan_reference: WP1 706-707 (manual link_hpc action for File→Open data); WP4 808-809, 824-825 (late viewers)
suggested_home: WP1 (manual link action) + WP4 (re-run pairing/time links when data are added)
rationale: Adding channels without restarting is natural in Glue. The missing part is coordinating late-added data, which the plan specifies for viewers but not for datasets.
verify_note: Runtime loading works, and WP1 plans a manual link action. Coordinating time links for datasets added after the preset is not specified. I verified the unverified TELESCOP point: a real AIA cutout has an empty TELESCOP, so File > Open skips the IRIS factory and uses Glue's generic FITS reader.

name: Slit-jaw / context cubes (SJICUBE, up to six)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Up to six FITS slit-jaw or context cubes (v1.7.3; earlier releases took one) with arbitrary nx, ny and nt can be given as sjicube=[...] or loaded via File > Open. Labels come from TELESCOP/TDESC1, parsed as IRIS SJI_xxxx or SDO channel names, and a combobox selects among them.
gap: Loading and selection exist with no channel limit, and the data collection replaces the combobox. Multi-SJI coordination (time sync, slit overlay) is still WP4 work. The browser auto-opens only the first image (iris.py:62-65).
glue_evidence: The scanner keys every SJI by TDESC1 and every AIA cutout by channel (glue_solar/sources/loaders/scan.py:164-165,174-175@main). The browser lists them all (sources/loaders/iris.py:240-242) and labels datasets from TDESC1 with irissji/sdoaia colormaps (loaders/iris.py:121-125).
suggested_home: Existing browser; WP4 for coordination
rationale: Several SJI channels plus AIA context is the core IRIS browsing input, and it already loads correctly.
verify_note: Every SJI and AIA cutout is keyed by TDESC1, listed in the browser and labelled with an irissji or sdoaia colormap, with no channel limit. It exists on glue-solar main (not core). The browser auto-opens only the first image.

name: SJI-formatted AIA / Hinode context cubes
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Co-aligned SDO/AIA and Hinode/SOT cubes written in the IRIS SJI Level-2 format (iris_getaiadata, ITN32 products) load as SJI or reference cubes. They appear with the IRIS slit overlaid, e.g. AIA 304 or SOT Ca II H.
gap: AIA cutouts load today. Hinode/SOT SJI-format cubes are unsupported by both irispy and the scanner, and the plan never mentions them. Drawing the IRIS slit on AIA context through WCS is not planned (WP4's slit is SJI-aux based; WP7 draws only the FOV).
glue_evidence: irispy 0.8.1 read_files loads INSTRUME AIA* files as AIACube and warns on and skips other INSTRUME values (io/utils.py:195-208; io/sji.py:239). The glue-solar scanner accepts only aia_l2_* AIA files (scan.py:110-115@main). Integer AIA cubes keep -200 fill values instead of NaN (io/sji.py:231-234). The WP4 slit overlay is built from the SJI 'slit x position' extra coordinate (wp4_common.py:16-29).
plan_reference: Capability boundary 356-358; WP1 716-718; WP7 928-936 (remote AIA, FOV polygon)
suggested_home: WP1 tests (AIA-cutout pairing) + WP4 (WCS-based slit/marker on linked context); SOT → upstream irispy / later item
rationale: AIA context with the slit overlaid is a common IRIS quicklook view. SOT cubes are rarer, so SOT support could wait.
verify_note: AIA cutouts load, and irispy warns on and skips any other INSTRUME. The plan has no Hinode or SOT mention, and the WP4 slit comes from SJI aux data, not WCS. A real cutout is int16 with BSCALE=1, so -200 fills stay integer but are masked. The INSTRUME value of an ITN32 SOT cube was not verified.

name: Reference image window
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Shows the reference data with its own zoom/pan, colour bar, cursor, and mask and raster overlays. It opens automatically when reference data are present.
gap: No colour bar exists and none is planned. Auto-opening a reference viewer is not part of WP4 (the prototype opens SJI/map/profile only, wp4_common.py:185-199). The raster/slit overlay is planned only on SJI (WP4 795).
glue_evidence: The Glue Image Viewer has per-viewer zoom/pan, subsets as mask overlays and stretch/contrast. Cursor readout comes from solar:cursor_readout (glue_solar/tools.py:69-127@main) or Qt #74 cursor_status (glue_qt/viewers/image/data_viewer.py@6b579814). There is no colour bar: `git grep -i colorbar` finds nothing in glue upstream/main 77dc9b88 glue/viewers or glue-qt origin/main.
suggested_home: WP4 preset; colour bar as a new solar tool or upstream glue-core/Qt feature
rationale: The viewer machinery exists. A colour bar matters for quicklook intensity reading and is unplanned everywhere.
verify_note: There is no colour bar in core or Qt, and the plan never mentions one. An upstream request has been open for years (glue issue #1087, 'Add colorbar to image viewer'). WP4 does not auto-open a reference viewer.

name: Reference detailed-spectrum and spectrum-time windows
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: In dual-cube mode, the reference data gets its own detailed-spectrum and spectrum-time windows, drawn by a separate plotting path.
gap: Every dataset already has this machinery, but the WP4 preset covers only rasters[0] (wp4_common.py:187-199). Tying a second window's spectrum and time–wavelength views to the same selected point depends on WP1 raster/raster links and WP4 fixed-index coordination, and neither names a multi-window layout.
glue_evidence: A Profile viewer works on any dataset, and time–wavelength images come from axis selection (review_20260923/test_existing_workflows.py:62,184; plan 500-528). Raster-to-raster links need the WP1 wrapper (review_20260923/README.md:19-25: 0 links on main, 1 with WP1).
suggested_home: WP4 (multi-window preset) + WP1 (raster/raster links)
rationale: IRIS observations routinely have several lines of interest, such as Mg II with Si IV. Parallel spectral displays per window are the IRIS form of dual-cube mode.
verify_note: The machinery works on any dataset, but the WP4 preset covers only rasters[0], and raster/raster links need the WP1 wrapper (0 links on main, 1 with WP1). No multi-window layout is named anywhere in the plan.

name: Slit-jaw image windows
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: One window per SJI or context cube, titled with the instrument and channel. Each has its own zoom/pan sliders, colour bar, cursor and path/measurement overlays, and each can be toggled in the Displays tab.
gap: A slit overlay per SJI is planned, but the prototype opens only sjis[0] (wp4_common.py:185-186), so a one-viewer-per-channel preset is unspecified. Colour bar and measurement overlays are neither available nor planned.
glue_evidence: Any number of Image viewers can be opened, each titled by its dataset label (loaders/iris.py:121-125@main), with per-viewer zoom/pan. A 3D path tool exists ('slice', glue_qt/plugins/tools/pv_slicer/pv_slicer.py:11-30@origin/main). No colour bar or distance/measurement tool exists (git grep colorbar/ruler/measure on glue upstream/main and glue-qt branches: none).
suggested_home: WP4 (per-channel SJI viewers + slit overlay); colour bar/measure as a new item
rationale: SJI windows with the slit are central to IRIS CRISPEX browsing. The basic viewers exist, so the work is presets plus the overlay.
verify_note: Status and priority hold, but one evidence claim is wrong. Viewer windows are titled with the viewer LABEL ('2D Image'), or state.title if set, not the dataset label, so a preset must set state.title for channel titles. No distance or measure tool exists, and PV 'slice' is the only path tool.

name: Main vs reference (two-stream) blink
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: A separate window alternates the main and reference images (v1.5.5), also during playback (v1.6), labelled with the time. iris_ximovie offers Stream 1/Stream 2/Blink of two streams at the same frame, with mean-intensity normalisation. Plan WP5 layer blink covers the concept (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:857-864).
gap: Layer blink covers main versus reference only when both are layers in one viewer, with the reference reprojected through links. Mean-intensity normalisation, a per-layer time label and behaviour during playback are not specified.
glue_evidence: No blink exists in glue or glue-qt (`git grep -i blink` finds nothing on upstream/main, origin/main or the PR branches). The prototype BlinkTool cycles the visible data layers of one Image viewer on a QTimer (IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_blink.py:14-58). solar:frame_time labels only the reference data's time (glue_solar/tools.py:54-66@main).
plan_reference: WP5 854-859 (the feature text cites 857-864; the blink bullet is 854-859); keyboard 493
suggested_home: WP5 (layer blink)
rationale: The first milestone requires two-wavelength blink (447-450), not main/reference blink. This is a convenience on top of WP5.
verify_note: The WP5 layer blink (plan 854-859) cycles the visible layers of one viewer. A reference reprojected through links therefore gives main/reference blink, but not mean normalisation or per-layer time labels. The first milestone requires two-wavelength blink (447-450), not this.

name: Master time selection (Main / Reference / SJI)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: The Main, Reference or a chosen SJI dataset drives time. The master sets the cadence and range, and the others snap to their nearest-time frame (each SJI index is precomputed per main time). With an SJI as master, the SJI can be followed beyond the raster span. The plan asks for navigation from an explicit master with nearest-exposure matching (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:436-440).
gap: The WP4 tasks cover this. The prototype still has no explicit master selector and clamps beyond coverage, so following an SJI past the raster span waits on the no-match policy the plan requires.
glue_evidence: Glue sliders are per viewer, and glue/glue-qt have no cross-dataset time matching. The prototype link_time/nearest/sync_slices (IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp4_common.py:37-75,92-154) clamps outside coverage (lines 38,48) and follows whichever viewer moved last. Raster-map viewers never drive it (111-112). The #52 Time component exists (loaders/iris.py:81-84,112@main).
suggested_home: WP4
rationale: Nearest-exposure time sync driven by a master is the defining CRISPEX/IRIS coordination behaviour.
verify_note: The plan explicitly requires an explicit master, nearest-exposure matching and a no-match policy. The prototype has none of these: it clamps outside coverage, is driven by whichever viewer moved last, and step×slit map viewers never drive it.

name: Raster timing offset
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: The 'Raster timing offset [raster position]' slider chooses which raster step's time represents a raster frame when matching SJI and reference frames. It defaults to the step closest to CRVAL4. It exists because each step within a raster has its own time.
gap: The plan asks for a defined 4D mapping, but it has no user-selectable representative raster step (CRISPEX's timing offset) and no default, such as the mid-raster or CRVAL step, for frames that span the whole raster.
glue_evidence: The stack keeps a Time per (scan, step, slit) (stack_spectrograms.py:50-61; loaders/iris.py:112@main). The prototype maps SJI frames to (scan, step) (wp4_common.py:57-66) but returns early for step×slit map viewers (wp4_common.py:111-112), so a whole-raster frame never picks a representative step.
suggested_home: WP4 (time-matching policy)
rationale: On long rasters the step chosen changes which SJI frame is shown by minutes. The policy needs an explicit knob or default.
verify_note: Per-step times are retained, but there is no representative-step knob or default for whole-raster frames. The reverse direction (raster map drives SJI) is not implemented in the prototype.

name: Per-raster-step 'Local' timing readout
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: When the time array varies with raster step, a 'Local (UTC)' row shows the exposure time of the raster step under the cursor, for both main and reference data.
gap: No WP bullet shows the exposure time of the raster step under the cursor. Extending cursor_status or the solar readout to read the Time component would provide it.
glue_evidence: solar:frame_time shows a min–max range when the displayed frame spans several exposures (glue_solar/tools.py:54-66@main). Qt #74 cursor_status reports only the position and the reference layer's value (glue_qt/viewers/image/data_viewer.py cursor_status@6b579814). A per-pixel Time component exists (loaders/iris.py:81-84,112).
suggested_home: WP4 (readouts) via glue_solar/tools.py
rationale: Scanning rasters mix space and time. A cursor-local time is the cheap way to make that visible.
verify_note: solar:frame_time shows a min–max range, and both cursor readouts show only position and the layer value. No WP bullet adds the exposure time under the cursor.

name: Assemble repeated rasters into a 4D time series
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: All raster files of an observation are stacked into an (x,y,lambda,t) cube, and each exposure's time since DATE_OBS is stored as an (nx,ntime) array (ntime=1 for a single repeat). Capability: repeated rasters as one 4D cube with an acquisition time for every raster step.
gap: The capability itself is complete. Its limits (scan-0 WCS, equal shapes, stack meta keeping only scan 0's exposure times) are tracked under F115 and F117.
glue_evidence: raster_data(stack=True) builds a (scan, step, slit, wavelength) float memmap with a per-pixel datetime64 Time (glue_solar/sources/loaders/stack_spectrograms.py:14-84; loaders/iris.py:104-113,153-175@main). The map-1 probe built a 3-scan Si IV stack of shape (3, 8, 109, 29).
suggested_home: Existing (glue-solar main)
rationale: This is the in-memory equivalent of the Level-3 cube, consistent with the Level-3 non-goal.
verify_note: Reproduced: a 3-scan 2014 C II stack loaded as (3, 8, 109, 17) with a per-pixel datetime64 Time. It exists in glue-solar main, not core.

name: Multiple raster files with a file slider (per-scan coordinates)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Given a raster sequence (e.g. 180 files from iris_find_file), a 'File no.' slider steps between rasters, each keeping its own coordinates. glue-solar's 4-D stack uses scan 0's WCS, and per-scan WCS is deferred (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:387,1014-1016).
gap: Per-scan WCS inside the stack is deferred with no schedule. Separate per-scan datasets have correct coordinates but no shared stepping control.
glue_evidence: Per-scan datasets keep their own WCS (loaders/iris.py:115-117@main). The stack uses scan 0's WCS (stack_spectrograms.py:36,73). Glue has no slider that steps between separate datasets.
suggested_home: Deferred per-scan stack WCS item (WP1 follow-up)
rationale: CRISPEX itself uses one WCS per cube, so scan-0 nominal WCS is adequate for a first quicklook.
verify_note: Per-scan WCS inside the stack is explicitly deferred with no schedule. The stack's Scan slider already steps between rasters on the scan-0 WCS.

name: Multi-exposure-per-position programs (NEXP_PRP > 1)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: For programs with several exposures per raster position, xdetector, xwhisker and xmap show separate 'Exp # at rast. pos.' and 'Raster position' sliders. The raster browser uses radio buttons to choose which exposure time is shown. The plan does not discuss these programs.
gap: Exposure-within-position is not separated from raster position, and there is no exposure selector. The WCS inverse with repeated positions is unverified.
glue_evidence: irispy only exposes NEXP_PRP as a meta property (irispy 0.8.1 meta.py:348-353). It builds one -TAB row per exposure from XCENIX (io/spectrograph.py:56-76), so repeated exposures appear as extra 'steps'. glue-solar has no handling (loaders/iris.py@main). Not verified on real NEXP_PRP>1 data because no fixture exists.
plan_reference: none ('NEXP' does not appear in the plan)
suggested_home: New WP4 sub-task, possibly an upstream irispy reshape
rationale: These programs are uncommon but would currently show misleading step axes. Record them as a known limitation at least.
verify_note: 'NEXP' does not appear in the plan. irispy only exposes NEXP_PRP as meta and builds one -TAB row per auxiliary exposure row. Behaviour on real NEXP_PRP>1 data remains unverified because there is no fixture.

name: Per-exposure readouts (exposure time, PZT offsets, pointing)
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Labels update with each frame's exposure time, time since start, PZTX/PZTY offsets and Xcen/Ycen. A tutorial asks why SJI intensity drops at frame 48, and the companion exercise asks whether AEC changed EXPTIMES; the cause was not verified. The plan asks to show each panel's exposure time (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:427), and Qt #52 adds a frame-time readout, but PZT offsets are not mentioned.
gap: Showing the exposure time is an acceptance criterion with no WP bullet. PZT and pointing readouts are absent, and stacks lose the exposure times of scans after the first. The feature text credits 'Qt #52', but the frame-time readout is glue-solar #52 (plan 102-104).
glue_evidence: Per-frame exposure time, pztx/pzty and xcenix/ycenix are irispy SJI extra_coords (io/sji.py:191-220), but glue-solar keeps only data, mask and Time components (loaders/iris.py:72-85@main; the probe listed exactly these for SJI_1400). The stack meta holds scan 0's (8,) exposure times for a (3,8,109,29) stack (stack_spectrograms.py:80; probe).
suggested_home: WP1 loader (carry per-exposure aux as components) + WP4 readout
rationale: Automatic exposure control (AEC) can change exposure times mid-observation. Without per-frame exposure time, intensity jumps are hard to interpret.
verify_note: Reproduced: SJI datasets carry only the data, mask and Time components, although irispy has per-frame exposure time, pztx/pzty and xcenix/ycenix. The stack meta keeps scan 0's (8,) exposure times. The feature text's 'Qt #52' is really solar #52.

name: Nearest-in-time SJI panel with consistency check
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: A raster-browser column shows a selectable SJI channel at the frame whose mid-exposure is nearest the selected raster exposure. It is cropped to the raster's Y range and zoom, titled with UT and exposure, and marks the selected pixel with a box. It reports 'SJI and slit coordinates not consistent' when the pixel falls outside the SJI FOV. Plan WP4 covers nearest-exposure matching and the slit overlay (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:436-440,491,789-800) but not this sanity check.
gap: The nearest SJI and the slit overlay are planned. There is no explicit warning when the selected pixel falls outside the SJI FOV, and cropping the SJI panel to the raster FOV or zoom is not planned.
glue_evidence: The prototype has nearest-exposure links and a slit subset (IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp4_common.py:16-75). WCS-linked Pixel subsets place markers on the linked data, but off-footprint values can be NaN (review_20260923/README.md:27-33). No FOV-consistency message exists in glue or glue-solar.
suggested_home: WP4
rationale: The core is planned. The sanity check is a small addition that stops a blank marker from being misread as a match.
verify_note: Nearest-exposure matching and the slit overlay are planned. There is no FOV-consistency warning, and off-footprint linked values can be NaN, so a blank marker is possible.

name: SHOW MOVIE from the raster-browser SJI panel
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Opens iris_sji->ximovie centred on the current SJI frame, with a chosen number of frames (11 to 5001 or all; the default is about 10 minutes) and a duration label, cropped to the current zoom. Glue playback exists; sequence selection and export are a later extension after WP5 (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:493).
gap: Playing N frames around the current one, or a detachable movie view, appears only as an unscheduled 'later solar extension'.
glue_evidence: Slice playback loops over the full axis and wraps (glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:81-83,146-197@origin/main). There is no frame-range or movie window.
suggested_home: Deferred movie/sequence item
rationale: Full-axis playback within the current zoom already gives most of the value.
verify_note: Playback covers the full axis and wraps. N-frame range selection is only an unscheduled later extension.

name: xsji_image single-channel SJI viewer
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Shows one magnified SJI channel with an exposure slider, a UT label, log(image), rotation to solar orientation, PS/JPG export and a button that opens ximovie. The Glue Image Viewer with a time slider and the #52 frame-time readout covers most of this (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:384).
gap: Rotation to solar north is unavailable, because the viewer shows the reference pixel grid, and the plan does not mention it. It matters only for rolled observations.
glue_evidence: The Image viewer has a time slider and playback (data_slice_widget.py:81-197@origin/main) and a log stretch (glue/config.py:839-842 in 1.27.0). The UT label is solar:frame_time (glue_solar/tools.py:21-66@main). mpl:save (glue_qt/viewers/matplotlib/toolbar.py:67-75) writes jpg/ps/eps/pdf/png; the Agg filetype probe lists eps, jpg and ps.
suggested_home: Existing; rotation as a new optional item
rationale: Covered apart from rotation, which is rarely needed for IRIS.
verify_note: Slider, playback, log stretch, the frame_time UT label and ps/eps/jpg export all exist. Only rotation to solar north is missing, and the plan does not mention it. The Agg canvas also writes gif, which answers the ximovie GIF format too.

name: SJI thumbnails that open the SJI viewer
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: iris_xcontrol shows up to four SJI channel thumbnails (NUV1/2, FUV1/2); clicking one opens xsji_image for that channel. glue-solar lists the SJI channels of each observation (audit:119).
gap: There are no image thumbnails, but choosing a channel and opening it works. Thumbnails are not in the plan.
glue_evidence: The browser lists each observation's SJI channels as checkboxes (glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:240,262-267@main; scan.py:164-165). Loaded datasets open from Glue's data collection, and only the first image auto-opens (sources/iris.py:62-65).
suggested_home: WP8 browser (optional)
rationale: A UI nicety, not a quicklook capability.
verify_note: Channels are listed as checkboxes, and loaded datasets open from the data collection. There are no thumbnails, and only the first image auto-opens, so 'exists' means choosing a channel and opening it, not thumbnails.

name: iris_sji2map SJI map-movie
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: Converts an SJI file into an SSW map array that movie_map can play. glue-solar loads SJIs as 3-D cubes (audit:128-129).
glue_evidence: SJI files load as 3-D Glue cubes with a gWCS time axis and playback (glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:121-142@main). irispy SJICube.to_maps (irispy 0.8.1 sji.py:298) can make sunpy maps if ever needed.
suggested_home: None needed
rationale: Glue's cube plus slider replaces a map-array movie.
verify_note: A 3-D SJI cube with a time slider and playback replaces a map-array movie, and irispy to_maps exists if ever needed.

name: Detector view (iris_xdetector) and CCD layout thumbnails
category: IRIS raster/SJI semantics, reference cubes & time sync
description: iris_xdetector shows the selected windows of one CCD group as wavelength x slit at a chosen exposure or raster position. iris_xcontrol's NUV/FUV thumbnails place each window at its detector position and open the view when clicked. Plan WP2 wraps irispy calculate_moments as a layer_action (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:726-737), without uncertainty or continuum outputs.

glue_evidence: irispy calculate_moments (irispy/utils/moments.py:33-209, .venv 0.8.1) returns only intensity, centroid, width (σ), velocity and velocity_width; grep for uncertainty/continuum finds nothing. The loader drops errors with read_files(uncertainty=False) at iris.py:141,147,174@236f0a8. Generic pixel-unit moments: glue/core/aggregate.py:8-50@1.27.0. Prototype: chk_wp2/wp2_moments_module.py:104.
suggested_home: WP2 (errors and continuum via irispy upstream)

The result is a solar-y x solar-x map, or solar-y x time for sit-and-stare. Plan WP2 wraps irispy calculate_moments with wing and rest-wavelength fields (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:731-737), and 'continuum' does not appear in the plan.

name: Double-Gaussian fit with red-blue asymmetry
description: A single fit runs first. Red-blue asymmetry over 5-100 km/s steps (summed over 30-50 km/s) then drives the double fit, and rb_mask records the number of components. Outputs are I/V/W and errors for two components, I(cont), the RB mask and the RB image. The plan defers RB asymmetry (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:1022-1024), although irispy 0.8.1 has calculate_red_blue_asymmetry (irispy/utils/red_blue.py:122).

plan_reference: WP6 IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:875-880; RB asymmetry deferred at :1022-1024
suggested_home: WP6, plus the deferred RBA layer_action

name: Window data with errors, calibration and binning (iris_getwindata)

name: Time-dependent SJI pointing and slit geometry
description: From SJI extension 1, CRISPEX reads the per-frame TIME, XCEN/YCEN, PC matrix and slit pixel (SLTPX1/2) columns and interpolates over zero-valued frames. The source recomputes SJI CRVAL/CRPIX/PC once, at the SJI frame closest to the main reference time, and does not update it per SJI frame. The SSTRED paper instead describes per-frame derivation, so the two disagree. This drives SJI coordinates and the slit overlay.

Zero-valued aux rows are interpolated only in _create_headers_wcs (sji.py:113-130), not in the gWCS used as cube.wcs (sji.py:240-242). The slit columns carry u.arcsec (sji.py:209-217), while WP4 treats them as pixels (wp4_common.py:16-22); the correct unit was not checked against an ITN.
plan_reference: WP4 per-frame slit subset IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:788-794; frame-0 pixel link vs last frame (42.2 arcsec) :566-575; D1 time-aware world link :629-633

The open slit-unit question is resolved by CRISPEX, which uses SLTPX1IX/SLTPX2IX as SJI CRPIX (pixels). WP4's pixel treatment is therefore right, and irispy's u.arcsec label looks wrong.

name: Animation speed and frame increment
description: Sliders set the animation speed (1-100 frame/s) and the frame increment. The same speed also sets the main/reference and spectral blink rate. iris_ximovie offers the same controls.
gap: There is no explicit fps control and no frame-increment option.
glue_evidence: Speed is set only by repeated forward/back presses (interval round(500/n) ms, glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:146-163). Each step is always ±1 (:186-193) @upstream/main. The archived audit noted the speed behaviour (archive/2026-09-05/IRIS_IDL_GLUE_CAPABILITY_AUDIT.md:216).
plan_reference: none (only the WP5 blink interval, IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:493)
suggested_home: upstream glue-qt slice widget
rationale: Coarse speed control exists. The increment matters mainly for very long series.
verify_note: Speed comes only from repeated presses (round(500/n) ms), each step is ±1, and there is no plan item.

name: Temporal range restriction
description: Editable lower/upper time indices, with Reset, restrict playback, the spectrum-time and space-time displays, and exports, e.g. to skip a start affected by cosmic rays. iris_ximovie has 'Restrict frame range'. The plan notes that stock Glue playback visits the whole axis and defers sequence selection (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:493).
gap: No work package owns a playback/display frame range for browsing; the plan mentions it only for movie export.
glue_evidence: Playback runs over the full slider range (glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:182-193). The λ–t display can be limited by y-limits/zoom (glue_qt/viewers/image/options_widget.ui:276-298).
suggested_home: upstream glue-qt slice widget (range) or WP4 addition
rationale: Skipping bad start frames and focusing on events is a common tutorial step for long IRIS series.
verify_note: Sequence selection appears only as an unscheduled 'Later solar extension' tied to movies. No work package owns a browsing or playback frame range.

name: DT and physical time-axis labelling
description: DT gives seconds per step; without it, the axes show frame numbers. For FITS, the time axis plus DATE_OBS/STARTOBS give UTC, and s/ms/hs units are normalised to seconds. IRIS per-step times (Level-3 extension 2) are irregular, so lambda-t and x-t axes need physical time that handles gaps.
gap: Raster step/exposure and stack scan axes are indices; UTC axes are only a pending WP4 decision.
glue_evidence: solar:frame_time shows the frame UTC (glue_solar/tools.py:21-66 @236f0a8). Qt #75 labels WCS time sliders with ISO times (data_slice_widget.py:40,74-78,132-135 @origin/slice-widget-time-axis 8852fcd1). The stack Scan axis is a LINEAR index (stack_spectrograms.py:66-73).
plan_reference: IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:144 (#75 limits), :427, :530-537 (index vs UTC), WP4 :817-818 ('Decide whether physical UTC axes are needed').
rationale: Exact times are already shown via readouts. Physical time axes matter most for irregular series (F090).
verify_note: frame_time readouts and Qt #75 (open draft) ISO slider labels exist. The stack Scan axis is a LINEAR index, and UTC axes are only a WP4 'decide whether' item.

name: Non-equidistant timing in spectrum-time display
description: A commit made after v1.7.4 (2019-04-04) handles non-equidistant timing in the spectrum-time diagram. It is in no tagged release.
gap: The plan says to preserve irregular sampling and gaps but only commits to deciding whether UTC axes are needed. There is no concrete task for a gap-aware λ–t axis.
glue_evidence: Image axes are pixel-indexed, so λ–t images space samples evenly (stack Scan WCS cdelt=1 at stack_spectrograms.py:66-73). Scatter can plot datetime components (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:488).
suggested_home: WP4
rationale: IRIS cadences have gaps (AEC, SAA), and index axes can mislead timing interpretation.
verify_note: The plan requires preserving irregular sampling and gaps, but has no concrete gap-aware lambda-t axis task.

name: Jump to a given UTC time
description: The IRIS-9 Python exercise finds the SJI timestep at 2014-11-07T16:19:07.8 and the raster file closest to that time. Capability: jump every dataset to a given UTC time.
gap: No 'go to UTC' control acts on the master dataset and propagates to all datasets. #75 helps only SJI-type WCS time axes.
glue_evidence: Qt #75 parses typed ISO text to the nearest frame (data_slice_widget.py:150 @origin/slice-widget-time-axis); upstream/main parses float only (:138). Raster/stack time is a data component, not a WCS axis, so it cannot be typed.
suggested_home: WP4 (time-sync controller input) + Qt #75
rationale: Jumping to a flare or context time is a standard IRIS task. The sync machinery is already planned, so the input control is small.
verify_note: #75 parses typed ISO text to the nearest frame on WCS time axes, while upstream parses floats only. Combined with WP4's planned master-driven sync, a typed SJI time could propagate, but there is no explicit 'go to UTC' control.

name: Spectrogram animation ('Create Animation')
description: Plays the selected window's spectrogram through raster positions or exposures in iris_ximovie; ITN26 highlights it for following sit-and-stare evolution. Glue slider playback covers viewing (audit:216), but export is unscheduled (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:396).
gap: Viewing is covered. Movie export is unscheduled.

suggested_home: none for viewing; movie export as unscheduled candidate (plan :1062-1063)
rationale: Following sit-and-stare spectrogram evolution already works interactively.
verify_note: The default spectrogram view has a step/exposure slider and playback. Movie export is unscheduled.

name: Event-finding workflow (TR brightenings, flares)
description: Tutorial tasks find the strongest transition-region brightenings, sympathetic flares and compact brightenings by playing, pausing, locking on the event and zooming in. Capability: playback, wavelength navigation, lock and zoom working together.
gap: Needs the WP4 coordination (point to fixed indices, time sync) and the end-to-end demonstration at :452-456.

rationale: This is the integrated CRISPEX use case, and the first-milestone acceptance criteria encode it.

name: Session save / load (.cses)
description: File > Save session and Load session write or restore the whole state: cursor, zoom, displays, scaling, paths, overlays, measurement, Stokes and window sizes. Restoring reopens the windows and resets every control, with version checks.
gap: No gap beyond WP3. Native viewer state already stores limits, cmap, zoom, slices and subsets.

A map-3 probe on real fixtures (glue-core 1.27.0 + solar main) failed: SJI raised GlueSerializeError "Don't know how to serialize _GlueWCS", the raster raised TypeError (numpy.save on Quantity), and no file was written. git status stayed clean.
suggested_home: WP3

verify_note: I reproduced the failure: serializing the SJI raised GlueSerializeError for _GlueWCS, and the raster raised TypeError from numpy.save on a Quantity. git status stayed clean.

name: Automatic last-session save and reload
description: crispex_last_session.cses is written after start-up and on quit. LAST_SESSION, or passing a .cses file as imcube (v1.7.4), reloads it and overrides all other inputs.

suggested_home: upstream glue-qt (recent/auto session), or glue-solar startup_action after WP3

name: Preferences window
description: CRISPEX > Preferences (Ctrl+P) covers the start-up window, autoplay, auto-update of the slit spectrum and layout (window offsets, colours, line thickness, symbols, interpolation, preview). It also covers scaling defaults ('Use current values'), input/output paths, file naming and warnings. Settings are saved across sessions (v1.6), with Default, Cancel and Save buttons.
gap: No IRIS-specific defaults pane (e.g. default percentile, raster colormap, stacking), which is not in the plan.
glue_evidence: The Preferences dialog loads plugin panes (glue_qt/app/preferences.py:111-112; preference_panes registry glue_qt/config.py:41,218) and offers colours, theme and font (preferences.ui:146-264). Settings persist via glue/_settings_helpers.py:8 @1.27.0.
plan_reference: IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:333 (dialog clipping), :343 (macOS menu role); WP5/WP8 deliberately avoid persisted settings (:861, :970-971).
suggested_home: glue-solar preference_panes entry if defaults prove needed
rationale: Generic preferences exist. IRIS defaults are optional polish.
verify_note: The Preferences dialog loads plugin panes from the preference_panes registry. No IRIS pane is planned.

name: Main spectral position slider and stepping across windows
description: The always-visible 'Main spectral position' slider (updating live while dragged) and Shift+A/S step through the concatenated windows, moving only within the displayed and restricted ones. The main image, the spectrum and lambda-t markers, and the phi-slice all update. Tutorials ask what happens at a window boundary.
gap: Moving the image wavelength slider does not move a spectral-position marker in the Profile or on a lambda-t image; the plan does not ask for image->profile marker sync. Stepping across concatenated windows has no equivalent because each window is a separate dataset. No keyboard step shortcut.
glue_evidence: Per-dataset slider with first/prev/next/last, wrap and live drag: glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.ui:88-214, data_slice_widget.py:43,66,171-198@glue-qt main 9780eaf9. Navigate is one-way profile->image: glue_qt/viewers/profile/profile_tools.py:147-161; its line only moves on a profile press: mouse_mode.py:26-40@main. One Data per window/scan: glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:104-118@solar main 236f0a8.
plan_reference: IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:447-449 (spectrum->map navigation), 489 (Navigate row), 623-625 (Level-2, not the CRISPEX input format)
suggested_home: WP4/WP5 (bidirectional spectral-position marker); cross-window stepping is a non-goal under Level-2 loading
rationale: Stepping wavelength is the core CRISPEX action, and the slider already covers it for each window. Tying the current position into the spectrum and lambda-t panels is the missing piece. Window concatenation is a Level-3 artefact that the plan deliberately avoids.
verify_note: Each window's slider (first/prev/next/last, wrap-around, live drag) exists. Navigate only goes from profile to image: its line moves only when the profile is pressed. The plan has no marker that follows the image slider in the Profile or lambda-t view. Plan line 489 only adds 'image/point selection to profile slices'.

name: Default starting wavelength
description: CRISPEX starts at the first wavelength of the first window (Si IV continuum in the tutorial), so the main image looks black until the user moves to a line. Capability: a sensible default slice, such as a line core.
gap: No task sets the preset's initial wavelength slice to the line core or rest wavelength. The prototype's mid-index is only a heuristic.
glue_evidence: Image viewer default is slice 0 on every axis: glue/viewers/image/state.py:318-323@glue-core 1.27.0 (.venv). The WP4 prototype uses mid-window rather than the line core: IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp4_common.py:186-188. The rest-wavelength helper exists only as a prototype: wp5_units.py:11-24.
plan_reference: IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:485 ('useful axes/scaling' for the preset, no default slice); 846-849 (rest-wavelength priority); 1111-1113 (fixtures can omit TWAVE)
suggested_home: WP4 preset, using WP5 rest-wavelength helper (nearest pixel), with mid-window fallback when TWAVE is absent
rationale: Starting on a continuum pixel gives the same black first image that ITN26 warns about. The fix is small once WP5's rest helper exists.
verify_note: Core sets the default slices to 0, and the Qt slider syncs from that state. The WP4 prototype uses the middle index (line 193, not 186-188 as cited). No plan task sets the starting wavelength to the line core. For Level-2, slice 0 is the window edge, not the Level-3 Si IV continuum, so the effect is milder but real.

name: Reference spectral position and lock to main
description: A separate reference spectral-position slider (v1.5.6; Ctrl+A/S) chooses, for example, the AIA channel in a reference cube. 'Lock reference to main' ties the two positions together when refnlp equals nlp.
gap: An independent reference position works today. 'Lock reference to main' is absent, and the plan's keep-wavelength-independent rule effectively excludes it.
glue_evidence: Each Image viewer builds its own sliders for its reference data: glue_qt/viewers/common/slice_widget.py:64-135@main. SJI and AIA cutouts load as separate datasets: glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:121-125,240-242@solar main. The WP4 sync prototype moves only leading exposure axes: wp4_common.py:103-131.
plan_reference: IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:440 and 808-810 (keep wavelength/slit independent; do not move wavelength sliders)
suggested_home: Non-goal unless requested; optional WP5 toggle for two views of the same dataset
rationale: For IRIS the reference is usually SJI or AIA, stored as separate datasets whose nlp differs from the main cube, so a lock rarely applies. A separate viewer with its own slider already meets the need.
verify_note: Separate viewers have independent sliders, and SJI/AIA load as separate datasets. The lock is simply missing. Plan lines 440 and 808-810 only forbid moving wavelength sliders by accident during temporal sync; they do not exclude an explicit lock, so 'effectively excludes' overstates it.

name: Detailed spectrum window
description: Shows the spectrum at the cursor or locked pixel for the current frame, in one sub-panel per displayed window. The average spectrum is overplotted, with a y=0 line and markers for the current, Doppler-mirror and reference positions. A km/s top axis is drawn when velocities are available.
gap: Not planned: a current-position marker driven by the image slider, a y=0 line, Doppler-mirror/reference markers, a secondary km/s top axis (WP5 swaps the x unit instead) and per-window sub-panels. Plan text at 486/513 assumes Mean profiles, but the Profile default is Maximum, so the preset must set Mean explicitly.
glue_evidence: Probe map-4/test_map4_probe.py (core 1.27.0 + Qt 6b579814 + solar main, 3 passed): a Pixel subset profile equals raster[3,20,:], and the whole-data layer with Mean equals the nanmean average spectrum. The same probe printed 'default function maximum' (glue/viewers/profile/state.py:22-26,73@1.27.0). Velocity x-unit exists only as a prototype: wp5_units.py:27-44.
suggested_home: WP4 preset (function=Mean, per-window profiles) + WP5 markers/velocity
rationale: The detailed spectrum is the central CRISPEX panel. The data path is verified, but marker and overplot details are missing. The Maximum default makes the whole-cube overplot misleading.

WP4 line 804 already says to use mean profiles, and the prototype sets it (wp4_common.py:197). Not in the plan: draft core #2603 and Qt #73 add programmatic vertical-line layers in Profile viewers, which could serve as the current-position marker. #2603 draws horizontal lines only in Scatter/Image, so it cannot draw the y=0 line in a Profile.

name: Multiple IRIS spectral windows shown side by side
description: NWIN, WSTARTi, WWIDTHi and WDESCi define the spectral windows, and TWAVEi gives each window's reference wavelength. The windows appear side by side, with separator axes, in the detailed-spectrum, spectrum-time and slit-spectrum displays.

glue_evidence: One Data per window: glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:104-118@solar main. The WP4 quicklook opens only rasters[0]: IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp4_common.py:180-195. Raster/raster autolink gives 0 links on main and 1 with WP1: IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260923/README.md:19-25.
suggested_home: WP4 preset (one Profile/lambda-t viewer per selected window, tiled) after WP1
rationale: IRIS science compares C II, Si IV and Mg II. The acceptance text names multiple windows, but the prototype and WP4 bullets implement only one.

I probed two windows of one scan (C II 1336 and Mg II k 2796, 2014 sample): 0 links with the main wrapper plus #2595, and 1 WCSLink with the WP1 wrapper. So the WP1 dependency does hold. The WP4 bullets open only one raster.

name: Diagnostics (spectral window) visibility selection
description: The Diagnostics tab has 'Display all' plus a checkbox per main window (restored in v1.7.3), and a Display all/Hide combobox for reference windows. At least one window stays visible. IRIS-9 uses it to show only Mg II.

suggested_home: WP4 preset + WP9 docs
rationale: Choosing windows at load time already covers the IRIS-9 'Mg II only' use.
verify_note: The browser lists each window as a checkable child and loads only the ticked ones. Layer visibility then covers hiding at runtime.

name: Per-column wavelength-window menu (raster browser)
description: Each raster-browser column has a pull-down to choose any spectral window, plus a 'Current window' label. The plan requires selecting line windows with their own wavelength grids and scaling (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:447-448).

glue_evidence: Reference-data combo boxes: glue_qt/viewers/image/options_widget.ui:84 and glue_qt/viewers/profile/options_widget.ui:142@main. The viewer title tool is at glue_qt/viewers/common/tools.py:40. Changing reference data resets slices: glue/viewers/image/state.py:318-323@1.27.0.
suggested_home: WP4 preset / WP9 docs

name: Spectral/velocity range restriction (global or per window)
description: Low/high sliders restrict the displayed range for main or reference data, globally or per window (v1.7.4). They are in Doppler km/s ('Doppler minimum/maximum') when velocities exist, have a Reset button, and need not be centred on the line (v1.7.3), e.g. to show only blueshifts. Tutorials use it to show only Mg II or to include the Mg II triplet near 2798 Angstrom. ITN26 notes that it once worked only for single-line Level-3 files.
gap: Per-viewer display limits exist, and WP5 would make them settable in km/s. The plan does not restrict the image slider's stepping range or the lambda-t x-range to match. There is no global control across windows.
glue_evidence: Profile x_min/x_max text entry: glue_qt/viewers/profile/options_widget.ui:264-312@main. Reset via mpl:home: glue_qt/viewers/matplotlib/toolbar.py:51-65@main. x_display_unit: glue/viewers/profile/state.py:40-41@1.27.0. Velocity units exist only as a prototype: wp5_units.py:27-44.
suggested_home: WP5 (velocity limits) + WP9 docs; stepping-range restriction optional in WP4
rationale: Tutorials use this to focus on Mg II or blueshifts. Display limits cover most of it once WP5 lands.
verify_note: The Profile has x_min/x_max text fields and Home resets the limits. Velocity units exist only in the WP5 prototype. Nothing limits the range the image slider steps through.

name: Spectral (two-wavelength) blink
description: 'Start spectral blink' alternates the main image between the current position and a 'Position to blink against' (e.g. Mg II k3 against the Si IV or C II core) at the animation speed; tutorials use 1-3 frame/s. Plan WP5 has a two-wavelength blink (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:447-450,857-859).
glue_evidence: No blink in stock code: 'git grep -i blink' finds nothing in glue-qt origin/main and no blink feature in glue upstream/main. The WP5 prototype blinks layers only: IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_blink.py:14-63. The slider timer defaults to 500 ms: glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:81-83@main.
suggested_home: WP5

name: Spectrum plot y-range and plot styling
description: Editable lower/upper y-values for the main or reference detailed spectra, e.g. -0.01 to 0.1 to make the lines visible. Line thickness was added in v1.7.1 and better axis labelling in v1.6.
glue_evidence: y_min/y_max: glue_qt/viewers/profile/options_widget.ui:264,312@main and glue/viewers/matplotlib/state.py:127-128@1.27.0. Line width: glue/viewers/profile/state.py:349 and glue_qt/viewers/profile/layer_style_editor.ui:117. Label and tick sizes: glue_qt/viewers/matplotlib/axes_editor.ui:43-92,207.
suggested_home: WP9 docs only
rationale: Stock Profile options already cover this.

name: Per-window spectral multiplier
description: 'Multiply <window> by <value>' scales individual windows in the detailed spectrum, so faint C II or Si IV can be seen next to bright Mg II.
gap: There is no arbitrary numeric multiplier. With one viewer per window (F072), each window autoscales independently anyway.
glue_evidence: Normalize each layer to [0,1]: glue/viewers/profile/state.py:50-51,411-412@1.27.0 and glue_qt/viewers/profile/options_widget.ui:168. Per-layer v_min/v_max: layer_style_editor.ui:57-70@main.
suggested_home: Docs; none unless windows share one axis

name: Compare detailed spectrum with the average spectrum
description: 'Scale to maximum of average' (v1.5.2) and 'Subtract average' (fixed for Stokes other than I in v1.6) compare the local profile with the mean spectrum.

suggested_home: WP5 optional derived-profile option or docs (arithmetic attribute)
rationale: Useful but secondary for quicklook, and overplotting covers most of it.
verify_note: The plan has no subtract-average or scale-to-average control. The suggested arithmetic-attribute docs route is unverified: glue evaluates expressions on requested views, so an axis-reduced mean may be wrong. I did not test it.

name: Average-spectrum time range (MNSPEC)
description: Chooses the scan t, or the range [t0,t1], used to compute the in-program average spectrum (default t=0). The time-range option was added in v1.0.

suggested_home: WP9 docs / WP4 combination rule
rationale: Subsets already express this.
verify_note: An xrange selection on a Scan- or exposure-axis Profile, combined with a Mean profile, averages over the chosen scans. This works for a 4D stack or sit-and-stare data, but not for the default per-scan datasets, where each scan is a separate Data object.

name: Custom plot axis titles (XTITLE/YTITLE)
description: Custom x- and y-titles for the main and/or reference detailed-spectrum and spectrum-time plots. Labels from FITS headers cannot be overridden this way.

suggested_home: none

name: Warping of non-equidistant sampling (NO_WARP)
scope_note: NO_WARP: IRIS wavelength equidistant; irregular time handled by WP4 time axes
description: Spectrum-time diagrams with non-equidistant wavelength or time sampling are warped onto a linear axis (CRISPEX_GET_WARP; v1.5.3, optimised in v1.7.4). This is needed for irregular CRISP line positions. NO_WARP disables it, and INSTRUME='IRIS' turns warping off by default.
glue_evidence: The Image viewer renders index grids from any two axes: glue/viewers/image/state.py:326+ numpy_slice_aggregation_transpose@1.27.0. Irregular IRIS timing is handled as index-versus-UTC in the plan.
suggested_home: non-goal
